page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Cell Cycle and Cell Division · 2 marks

steps.label: The two phases
lines: The cell cycle has only two phases: interphase
and M phase, which is the division itself.
Interphase is the one that takes almost all the
steps.why: The question asks about phases of the CELL CYCLE, and there are only two of them, so the answer has to be one of these two. NCERT states that interphase lasts more than 95 per cent of the cycle.
common_mistakes: Naming M phase. Division proper is about one hour in a 24 hour cycle.
Naming S phase. S is a part of interphase, not a phase of the cell cycle.
steps.memory_tip: Two phases only: interphase and M phase. 23 hours against 1 hour.
steps.margin_note: One line. Name the two phases, then say which one is longer.

steps.label: The reason

lines.text: Interphase — it takes more than 95% of the cell cycle.

lines: In a human cell cycle of 24 hours, division takes
about 1 hour and interphase takes the other 23.
steps.why: The second mark is for the evidence, not for the name. This book's key answers 'Synthesis phase of Interphase'. S phase is a long stretch, but it is a sub-phase INSIDE interphase, and in a typical human cell G₁ (about 11 hours) is longer than S (about 8 hours) — so interphase is the answer that is right on both readings.
common_mistakes: Giving the name with no number. The second mark is for the 95 per cent or the 23 hours out of 24.
steps.memory_tip: 24 hours in the cycle: 23 for interphase, 1 for division.
steps.margin_note: Add one number. That is the second mark.

insider_note: The examiner wants the word interphase and one figure that proves it — more than 95 per cent, or 23 hours out of 24.
